egress.terms: Residential Proxies-GB is 'Pay per GB' with 'Rotating & sticky sessions'; the unlimited by-port product does not restrict traffic volume or the number of IPs, with bandwidth fixed by plan tier.

record.interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 forward proxy; residential, unlimited and SOCKS5 products accept username and password or IP whitelisting, static residential accepts username and password only; 'API reselling support' is listed on the GB product.
record.tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password or an allowlisted source address: curl -x, python requests, rclone --socks5, or a host-side hop for a runtime that cannot dial a proxy itself.
record.chaining: A host-side hop dials the vendor's HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials; the upstream sees an address from the vendor's pool in place of the caller's address.

record.category: per-address static residential proxy (native and broadcast)
record.tier: Static Residential Proxies, per IP, 7, 30 or 90 days

free_tier.stated: No free tier for the static product. Static Residential Proxies are sold per IP from $3.5 /IP, and the location list prices Native IPs at $3.50/IP, with the Dual NTT locations at $3.90/IP and a Comcast location at $4.90/IP; terms come in 7, 30 or 90 days. Volume discount: 5-9 IPs 2% off, 10-49 IPs 5% off, 50-199 IPs 10% off, 200-499 IPs 20% off. The same vendor also sells Residential Proxies-GB from $0.55 /GB (packs of 5 GB at $15 up to 500 GB+25 GB at $400), Mobile Proxies from $1.45 /GB and Unlimited Proxies by port from $1 /port.
free_tier.notes: The term-to-price mapping of the static list is not recoverable from the read: the page prints one $/IP figure for each location and the 7, 30 and 90 day durations are named only in the FAQ, so which term the printed price buys is unverified.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic pack, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not stored bytes. The lease term is 7, 30 or 90 days and an IP can be renewed before expiry to keep the same address.
retention.notes: days is null because no bytes are stored.

egress.terms: Unlimited bandwidth for static residential IPs: "no bandwidth or session limitations". The unit sold is an address for a term, not a byte.
egress.free_allowance: unlimited, stated as no bandwidth or session limitations

record.interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 proxy endpoints; static residential IPs authenticate by username and password only. The home page lists API access for the GB product and API reselling support; whether the static product has an API is unverified.
record.tooling: Any client that speaks SOCKS5 or an HTTP proxy. A Cloudflare Worker fetch() takes no proxy option, so the endpoint is reached through a relay that dials SOCKS5 for it. No vendor SDK or rclone backend; that is a note on tooling, not a reason to reject.
record.chaining: The upstream sees the leased address instead of a Cloudflare range. The Native label and the Dual NTT location names are the vendor's own words about registration; no delivered address was seen, so the registration class is unverified.

limits.value: one dedicated address per unit, unlimited traffic and sessions, with the term fixed at 7, 30 or 90 days and renewal before expiry to keep the address
none for the static product: bandwidth is stated as unlimited; the GB product is sold in packs from 5 GB to 500 GB+25 GB with validity of 30, 90 or 180 days

record.binding_note: Traffic is unlimited, so no byte quota fails first; what binds is the single address that carries everything and the registration class of that address, which the page labels but does not show.

identity_cost.detail: An account is needed before checkout; the sign-up page offers Google login and a form whose fields the reader did not render, so the exact identifiers (email, phone) are unverified: unverified, the sign-up form fields.
